By [the central limit theorem for MLEs](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/intro-MLEs.html#thm-dist-mle),
the [maximum likelihood estimates](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/intro-MLEs.html#def-mle) $\eb_k$ are approximately Gaussian
for large sample sizes;
see also the [table of Gaussian vs. MLE-based tests](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/intro-MLEs.html#tbl-gaussian-vs-mle-tests).

#### Wald test statistic

To test $H_0: \beta_k = \beta_{k,0}$ (typically $\beta_{k,0} = 0$):

$$z_k = \frac{\eb_k - \beta_{k,0}}{\HSE{\eb_k}}$$

Under $H_0$, $z_k \overset{\cdot}{\sim} N(0,1)$ for large $n$.

#### Confidence intervals for regression coefficients

A 95% [confidence interval](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/inference.html#def-confidence-interval) for $\beta_k$ is:

$$\eb_k \pm 1.96 \cdot \HSE{\eb_k}$$

#### Confidence intervals for exponentiated coefficients

By the invariance property of [MLEs](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/intro-MLEs.html#def-mle),
the MLE of $e^{\beta_k}$ is $e^{\eb_k}$.

A 95% [confidence interval](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/inference.html#def-confidence-interval) for $e^{\beta_k}$ is obtained by
exponentiating the endpoints of the CI for $\beta_k$:

$$
e^{\beta_k} \in \paren{
  e^{\eb_k - 1.96 \cdot \HSE{\eb_k}},\;
  e^{\eb_k + 1.96 \cdot \HSE{\eb_k}}
}
$$

For covariate coefficients ($k \neq 0$), $e^{\beta_k}$ is an [odds ratio](binary-outcome-associations.qmd#def-OR)
(the multiplicative change in [odds](binary-outcome-associations.qmd#def-odds) per 1-unit increase in $x_k$,
holding all other covariates fixed).
For the intercept ($k = 0$), $e^{\beta_0}$ is the baseline odds
(the odds when all covariates equal zero), not an odds ratio.

#### In R

In R, `parameters()` from the `parameters` package automatically computes
[Wald tests](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/intro-MLEs.html#def-wald-test) and [confidence intervals](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/inference.html#def-confidence-interval) for [logistic regression model](#def-logistic-regression) coefficients:

```{r}
#| label: tbl-beetles-wald-tests
#| tbl-cap: "Wald tests and 95% CIs for `beetles` logistic regression"
beetles_glm_ungrouped |>
  parameters() |>
  print_md()
```

Pass `exponentiate = TRUE` to `parameters()` to report
exponentiated coefficients.
The intercept is then interpreted as baseline [odds](binary-outcome-associations.qmd#def-odds),
while the non-intercept coefficients are [odds ratios](binary-outcome-associations.qmd#def-OR):

```{r}
#| label: tbl-beetles-wald-tests-OR
#| tbl-cap: "Exponentiated coefficients and 95% CIs for `beetles`"
beetles_glm_ungrouped |>
  parameters(exponentiate = TRUE) |>
  print_md()
```
